note: Plain-language explanations, applied automatically and identically to every party's quotes. Te reo Māori meanings follow Te Aka Māori Dictionary.

terms.def: Family, including extended family.
Food.
Land.
Sea or ocean.
Young people.
Elders.
People of the land: Māori as the Indigenous people of Aotearoa New Zealand.
The iwi or hapū with customary authority over a particular area.
Tribe; a Māori tribal group.
A Māori communal meeting place, including the meeting house and the open area in front of it.
The Māori language, an official language of New Zealand.
Guardian or caretaker, especially of the environment.
A Māori name for New Zealand.
The Māori-language text of the Treaty of Waitangi, signed in 1840 by the British Crown and many Māori rangatira (chiefs).
Self-determination or autonomy.
The government of New Zealand, especially as the Treaty partner of Māori.
A permanent commission of inquiry that hears Māori claims that Crown laws, policies or actions breached the Treaty, and makes recommendations.
The government agency that decides which medicines are publicly funded.
The Resource Management Act 1991, the main law for managing land use, building and environmental effects.
The New Zealand Emissions Trading Scheme, which puts a price on greenhouse gas emissions.
When the greenhouse gases released are balanced by those removed from the atmosphere. New Zealand law sets a 2050 target for most gases.
The 2019 law that sets New Zealand's emissions targets and created the Climate Change Commission.
An independent government body that advises the government and monitors progress towards low emissions and climate resilience.
The 2015 international climate agreement in which countries set targets to cut greenhouse gas emissions.
Companies that both generate electricity and sell it to households and businesses.
A voluntary, work-based savings scheme for retirement, with contributions from members, employers and the government.
Payments for families with children, paid through Inland Revenue.
Government-funded payments for parents taking time off work after a birth or adoption.
Inland Revenue, the government department that collects tax and runs student loans and Working for Families.
The Ministry of Social Development, which runs benefits and other social support through Work and Income.
A tax rule that stops landlords using losses on rental properties to reduce the tax on their other income.
A tax on the profit made when an asset, such as property, is sold.
Gross domestic product: the total value of goods and services produced in the economy.
Small and medium-sized businesses.
The main temporary work visa; employers must be accredited before hiring migrant workers on it.
A visa that lets a person live, work and study in New Zealand indefinitely.
A charge most international visitors pay when they apply for a visa or travel authority, used to fund tourism and conservation.
A government-backed scheme that lets eligible first home buyers borrow with a 5% deposit.
The co-operatives that own New World, PAK'nSAVE and Four Square supermarkets.
A market dominated by two companies; for groceries in New Zealand, Foodstuffs and Woolworths.
An Auckland body, set up by law, whose appointed members sit on some Auckland Council committees to represent Māori interests.
The law, in force since 2021, that allows assisted dying for eligible people with a terminal illness.
The Fast-track Approvals Act process, which lets selected projects get consents more quickly.
